To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dynamics of Br(3/2) and Br(1/2) formation in vinyl bromide and its perfluorovinylderivative have been investigated by photofragment imaging and state-selective [3+1] resonanceenhanced multiphotonionization technique at 234 nm.
the photodisscociation of vinyl bromide at 234 nm leads to the formation of Br atoms with a wide range of translational energy distributions.

the photodisscociation of perfluorovinylic bromide is more complicated than that of vinyl bromide due to the presence of the repulsive 3 A'(n,sigma*) state and the fluorination decreases the probability of intersystem crossing from triplet states to the electronic ground state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of Br( 2Pj) atoms produced from the C-Br bond cleavage of vinyl bromide (C2H3Br) and perfluorinated vinyl bromide (CF2=CHBr) upon 234-nm irradiation.
the dynamics of the photodisscociation process of vinyl and perflurovinyl bromides at 234 nm.
the dissociation dynamics of vinyl and perflurovinyl bromides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photodisscociation of vinyl bromide is a complicated process and that the photodisssociation of perfluoroviny bromide is even more complicated.
the Br(2P3/2) and Br( 2P1/2) are mainly produced from the triplet and singlet states, respectively.

the photodisscociation of vinyl bromide proceeds via the repulsive 3(sup 3)A' state with the formation of the Br(2P1/2) and Br(3P1/2), and via the 1A" and/or 3(sup n)A" states with the formation of Br(2PJ).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Br(2P1/2) formation is favored over Br(2P3/2) formation and the branching ratios of Br(2PJ) are dependent on the nature of the C-C bond.

the photodissocation of vinyl bromide at 234 nm proceeds through the repulsive 3B'(n,sigma*) state and the 1A'(pi,sigma*) state, whereas the 1A" (pi,sigma*) is responsible for the photodissocatation of perfluoroviny bromide.
the photodissocation of vinyl and perflurovinyl bromide is a complicated process, in which a large number of excited states contribute to the formation of the nascent Br atoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photodissocation dynamics of vinyl and perflurovinyl bromides are different in the sense of the Br atom formation.
the photodisscociation dynamics of perfluoroviny bromide is very different from that of vinyl bromide.
the Br(2P3/2) and Br( 2P1/2) formation is not a simple process.
